maria: ran an nsys capture on stage after the kernel-selector change, timeline looks like kernels are no longer overlapped; huge serialized gaps around KV eviction

 tj: can you paste the timeline link? did you include NVTX markers?

 maria: https://perf.redwood/nsys/1945012345 (trace uploaded to perf bucket)

 maria: NVTX markers were present, see span `KV::evict` followed by repeated tiny kernels `kv_eviction_shard_*` that used to be merged into one big kernel

 sam: oof, that smells like a batching heuristic / kernel fusion regression -> we've lost concat/merge step

 maria: numbers: before change we saw one `batch_merge` ~11ms. after change we see ~40 launches totalling ~62ms + ~15ms idle gaps in between

 lee: any chance the selector now forces stream sync? check for new `cudaStreamSynchronize` or `cuEventSynchronize` calls added in the patch

 maria: grep in runtime, found commit 9f4b2c8 removed `allow_async_eviction` and switched to per-shard kernel selection in `selector.cpp`

 tj: please run a git bisect with a tiny repro + nsys capture. I can spin up CI bisect too if you push a repro script

 infra-bot: bisect job queued: /ci/bisect/1945012345 - status: queued

 sam: local repro steps I used: `./runner --model small --batch 8 --prefix-cache --trace-kv` then `NSYS_NVTX=1 nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o trace ./runner --...`

 maria: pasted a trimmed nvprof-like timeline snippet for quick eyeballing:
```
NVTX: KV::evict [t=0ms]
kernel: kv_eviction_shard_0 [t=1ms]
kernel: kv_eviction_shard_1 [t=2ms]
...
kernel: kv_eviction_shard_39 [t=25ms]
NVTX: KV::evict_end [t=26ms]
```

 tj: hypothesis: selector changed kernel granularity to per-shard to reduce register pressure, but forgot to schedule them on different streams -> they run serially on default stream and cause gaps

 lee: also check whether `launch_bounds` or `maxThreadsPerBlock` changed; smaller kernels can increase kernel-launch overhead. and verify we didn't accidentally call any blocking host sync while enqueuing kernels

 maria: ran git bisect locally: first bad commit: 9f4b2c8 (author: anika) — reverting that locally restores the fused kernel and end-to-end latency drops ~1.8x on the repro

 sam: great, file an issue with the bisect result + attach nsys trace and the minimal repro steps. I'll assign to @lee for the follow-up fix and test additions

 maria: filing now: https://issues.redwood/INC-6721 attached perf-bkt/kv-1945012345.nsys and the diff from bisect

 lee: i'll open a PR to reintroduce the async-eviction path and make the selector fall back to fused kernel when beneficial. i'll also add an nsys-based CI test that fails if kernel launches > threshold for the small repro

 tj: can we also add a lightweight perfetto metric to alert on inter-kernel gaps > 2ms on CI traces? that would've caught this earlier

 maria: good idea — i'll add a perfetto rule to the CI collector template

 sam: putting on the perf board under "runtime regressions" and flagging as P1 for Dedicated customers. thanks for the quick triage everyone :thumbsup:
